precepts.text: Servants, be subject to your masters with all fear, not only to the good and gentle but also to the froward, to those that are like Nabal; enduring grief wrongfully for conscience toward God is thankworthy.
precepts.point: She did not turn her lord over to be destroyed, as some women today would be ready to do; instead she pleaded, Let not my lord regard this man of Belial, even Nabal: for as his name is, so is he; Nabal is his name, and folly is with him. She had not seen the young men David sent, or she would have stepped in then to protect their house.

note.label: 1 Samuel 25: Nabal's Folly and Abigail's Wisdom

precepts.why:
“Servants, be subject to your masters with all fear; not only to the good and gentle, but also to the froward.” The froward are those that are like Nabal. “For this is thankworthy, if a man for conscience toward God endure grief, suffering wrongfully.”

Abigail fell at David's feet and said, “Upon me, my lord, upon me let this iniquity be.” She was not the one who did anything wrong, but she took that iniquity upon herself. She was being that pillar of her house, using wisdom to protect it, for the scripture says she was a woman of good understanding.

She did not turn her lord over to be destroyed, as some women today would be ready to do. She pleaded, “Let not my lord, I pray thee, regard this man of Belial, even Nabal: for as his name is, so is he; Nabal is his name, and folly is with him: but I thine handmaid saw not the young men of my lord, whom thou didst send.” Had she seen them, she would have stepped in then to protect their house.

precepts.text: Likewise, ye wives, be in subjection to your own husbands, that if any obey not the word, they may without the word be won by the conversation of the wives, beholding your chaste conversation coupled with fear; this is what Abigail was putting in place.
precepts.point: She did not turn her lord over to be destroyed, as some women today would be ready to do; instead she pleaded, Let not my lord regard this man of Belial, even Nabal: for as his name is, so is he; Nabal is his name, and folly is with him. She had not seen the young men David sent, or she would have stepped in then to protect their house.

note.label: 1 Samuel 25: Nabal's Folly and Abigail's Wisdom

precepts.why:
“Likewise, ye wives, be in subjection to your own husbands; that, if any obey not the word, they also may without the word be won by the conversation of the wives; While they behold your chaste conversation coupled with fear.” This is what Abigail was putting in place.

Her chaste conversation was her behavior. When she heard David was coming, she made that feast and brought it down to meet him, to spare her house: “she hasted, and lighted off the ass, and fell before David on her face.”

That is the lesson for wives. If your lord is out of the spirit, instead of going railing for railing with him, your behavior should be able to win him over, to make him say, I am tripping, I have a good wife keeping the commandments who stays in a humble spirit. Provoking with the mouth just leaves an unhappy household, where people living under the same roof are set against each other.

Are You A Strong Independent Woman?

points: And David said to Abigail, Blessed be the Lord God of Israel, which sent thee this day to meet me. Wait — his what? I thought the woman had to be shut up and she cannot give any advice.

And then the argument was, well, what if the husband is wrong? What if he is in sin? That goes back to what I said earlier: the subjection in all things is not that he can tell you to sin. That is the one line, and it makes sense — it says obey God. But it is funny how they will use that and say I have got to listen to my husband who said do this, which was a sin, but then will not apply the behaviours, the laws she needs to apply as a wife, and therefore she is in sin. It is a sin, sisters, if you do not apply the laws of a wife. Every time you are disrespectful to him, every time you speak out of turn, every time you abandon those principles, you are in sin. And remember, you do not justify sin. There is no context for justification of sin.

note.label: SHE REVERENCE HER HUSBAND: Submission, Grace & Self-Examination of a Biblical Wife

points: Submission does not mean a woman cannot give advice to her husband. When she knows how, when and what to say, and in what spirit, it is valuable. Especially if she is involved in the body. That is a big one — you have a lot, especially amongst leadership wives, anybody that has rank, where the wives want to sit on their husband's rank and not make their own name and their own works. They just want to sit pretty on that.

And blessed be thy advice, and blessed be thou, which hast kept me this day from coming to shed blood, and from avenging myself with mine own hand. So Abigail was intelligent, decisive, articulate and courageous. She gave David counsel that prevented bloodshed.

note.label: SHE REVERENCE HER HUSBAND: Submission, Grace & Self-Examination of a Biblical Wife

points: Some of you women that want to serve the Lord are attached to some wicked men. On Clubhouse a lot of women say, we listen to you guys, but our husband is wicked. Here is a woman married to a wicked man: Nabal disrespected King David, and King David was coming to kill him.

Abigail told David, Let not my lord regard this man of Belial: Belial means a child of Satan. She said openly, my husband is the devil the Bible speaks of, and folly is with him. She wasn't defending him. Every wise woman that was with a wicked man wasn't taking him by the hand and following his plan.

note.label: Are You A Strong Independent Woman?

points: She told him, the Lord will certainly make my lord a sure house, because my lord fighteth the battles of the Lord; you're going to overcome, you're going to be king again. This is a woman who knows how to speak and how to deal with situations, cuz King David was coming to kill everything moving.

note.label: Are You A Strong Independent Woman?

points: David said, Blessed be thy advice, and blessed be thou, which hast kept me this day from coming to shed blood. The Lord put the spirit on her, she spoke eloquently, and he changed his mind. This is why it's important for women to know how to speak, when to speak, and how to speak.

note.label: Are You A Strong Independent Woman?

points: She told Nabal nothing till the morning light, cuz he was drunk; when the wine was gone out of him and she told him, his heart died within him, and about ten days after, the Lord smote Nabal that he died. Sometimes you got to let God handle your beef. Like with the SPLC, the Lord is going to return their wickedness on their own head.

note.label: Are You A Strong Independent Woman?

points: David sent and communed with Abigail, to take her to him to wife, and she bowed herself and said, let thine handmaid be a servant to wash the feet of the servants of my lord. Even attached to a wicked man, she still was in a place of humility. Some of you are not wicked; you're getting the title because of who you're attached to. Read your Bible and make your decision; draw your strength from the scripture.
